title: Global comparison transport agrees with compactification charts
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring and let
$$\begin{array}{ccc}X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\ f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\ Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y\end{array}$$
be Cartesian, with $f$ separated of finite type and $g$ arbitrary [def-cbc-compact-support-square, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Use the bounded-below constant-module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. For each corner $T$ let $A_T=\nu_T^*$, $B_T=R\nu_{T,*}$, and let $\eta_T:\operatorname{id}\xrightarrow{\sim}B_TA_T$ be the comparison unit [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. Write $l_u=u_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}$, $p_u=u_{\mathrm{proet}}^{-1}$ and $a_u:A_Ul_u\xrightarrow{\sim}p_uA_V$ for $u:U\to V$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations, lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. Let $H_f,H_{f'}$, $E:l_gH_f\to H_{f'}l_{g'}$, $r_V$ and $q_c$ be any simultaneous extension data with precisely the naturality, restriction and compactification normalization of [lem-cbc-etale-local-compact-support-extension]. No invertibility of $E$ is assumed.

On the full subcategories of etale-origin objects (objects isomorphic to $A_TM$ for some $M$) put
$$F_f=A_YH_fB_X,\qquad F_{f'}=A_{Y'}H_{f'}B_{X'},\qquad C_{f,L}=A_YH_f(\eta_{X,L}):A_YH_fL\xrightarrow{\sim}F_fA_XL,$$
and define $C_{f',M}$ likewise. The following maps are natural isomorphisms:
$$S_L=p_g(C_{f,L})\circ a_{g,H_fL},\qquad T_L=F_{f'}(a_{g',L})\circ C_{f',l_{g'}L}.$$
The morphisms
$$\Phi_L=T_L\circ A_{Y'}(E_L)\circ S_L^{-1}:p_gF_fA_XL\longrightarrow F_{f'}p_{g'}A_XL$$
form a natural transformation in $L\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$.

They have the following compactification normalization, including after restriction to any open $V\subseteq Y$ with $V'=g^{-1}V$. Work on that restricted square and suppress the restriction subscripts. Suppose $c=(j,p)$ is a compactification of $f$ with $j$ quasi-compact, and $c'=(j',p')$ is its pullback. Put $H_c^e=Rp_*^ej_!^e$, $H_c^p=Rp_*^pj_!^p$, and similarly for $c'$. For $N\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ use the canonical proper and open comparison isomorphism
$$C_{c,N}=Rp_*^p(e_{j,N})\circ b_{p,j_!^eN}:A_YH_c^eN\xrightarrow{\sim}H_c^pA_XN,$$
where $b_p$ is the normalized direct-image comparison [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image, lem-weil-pbc-transport-identifies-exchange] and $e_j$ is the degreewise natural extension-by-zero comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison, lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact, lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. Write $E^c:l_gH_c^e\to H_{c'}^el_{g'}$ for [def-cbc-exchange-map] and define
$$S^c_L=p_g(C_{c,L})\circ a_{g,H_c^eL},\quad T^c_L=H_{c'}^p(a_{g',L})\circ C_{c',l_{g'}L},\quad \Phi^c_L=T^c_L\circ A_{Y'}(E^c_L)\circ(S^c_L)^{-1}.$$
Let $M=l_{g'}L$, and set
$$D_{c,L}=C_{c,L}\circ A_Y(q^f_{c,L})\circ C_{f,L}^{-1},$$
$$J_L=H_{c'}^p(a_{g',L})\circ D_{c',M}\circ F_{f'}(a_{g',L})^{-1}.$$
Then the global transported transformation has exactly the local compactification formula under these endpoint identifications:
$$J_L\circ\Phi_L\circ p_g(D_{c,L})^{-1}=\Phi^c_L.$$
For an open restriction, the endpoint identifications from a global object to the restricted formulas are obtained from $r_V$, $a$ for the open inclusions, and $C_f,C_{f'}$. The displayed equality holds with these identifications inserted, and these identifications are compatible with iterated open restriction. This assertion identifies specified transformations; it asserts neither that $E_L$ nor that $\Phi_L$ is invertible.

proof.text: Use the constant-module categories and bounded-below derived categories of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. The exact comparison $A_T$ induces a functor on these categories, and [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] supplies the natural isomorphism $\eta_T:\mathrm{id}\cong B_TA_T$. Thus $C_{f,L}=A_YH_f(\eta_{X,L})$ is a natural isomorphism: its inverse is $A_YH_f(\eta_{X,L}^{-1})$. The same applies to $f'$. In particular the functors $F_f,F_{f'}$ and these comparisons are defined on the stated etale-origin objects. No compactification is chosen in this step.

source.place: Transport paragraph: the fully faithful comparison

proof.text: The isomorphism $a_u$ is natural by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. Functors preserve inverses, so the displayed $S,T$ are natural isomorphisms; explicitly $S_L^{-1}=a_{g,H_fL}^{-1}\circ p_g(C_{f,L}^{-1})$ and $T_L^{-1}=C_{f',l_{g'}L}^{-1}\circ F_{f'}(a_{g',L}^{-1})$. This also shows $p_{g'}A_XL$ is of etale origin, since $a_{g',L}$ identifies it with $A_{X'}l_{g'}L$, so every evaluation of $F_{f'}$ is in its domain.

The supplied exchange $E:l_gH_f\to H_{f'}l_{g'}$ is natural by [lem-cbc-etale-local-compact-support-extension]. For a morphism $t:L\to L_1$, its naturality is $H_{f'}l_{g'}(t)\circ E_L=E_{L_1}\circ l_gH_f(t)$. Apply $A_{Y'}$ and substitute the naturality equations for $S^{-1}$ and $T$. The resulting equation is $F_{f'}p_{g'}A_X(t)\circ\Phi_L=\Phi_{L_1}\circ p_gF_fA_X(t)$, proving the asserted natural transformation without inverting $E$.

source.place: Transport paragraph: functoriality of the transported map

proof.text: Now assume a chart $c=(j,p)$ as in the statement, on the global square or on any specified open restriction; its pullback $c'$ is a chart by [def-cbc-compact-support-square]. The proper maps $p,p'$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated: proper means separated and finite type, finite type includes quasi-compactness, and a separated morphism is quasi-separated [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated], with the conventions of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Thus [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] applies to these maps. Use its normalized $b_p$ as specified in [lem-weil-pbc-transport-identifies-exchange]. The comparison $e_j$ of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] extends degreewise: the comparison inverse image is exact, and the two extensions by zero preserve quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact, lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. Consequently $C_{c,N}=Rp_*^p(e_{j,N})\circ b_{p,j_!^eN}$ is a natural isomorphism, as is $C_{c',M}$. Their composites with $a_g,a_{g'}$ give natural isomorphisms $S^c,T^c$.

source.place: Transport paragraph: direct-image and extension-by-zero comparisons

proof.text:
Put $q=q^f_c$, $q'=q^{f'}_{c'}$, and $M=l_{g'}L$. These are natural isomorphisms by [lem-cbc-etale-local-compact-support-extension]. Naturality of $a_g$ in [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] gives
$$S^c_L A_{Y'}(l_gq_L)=p_g(C_{c,L})p_g(A_Yq_L)a_{g,H_fL}=p_g(D_{c,L})S_L.$$
The extension interface's chart normalization says precisely
$$q'_M E_L=E^c_L(l_gq_L),$$
where $E^c$ is the compactification formula of [def-cbc-exchange-map]. Here $q'_M:H_{f'}M\to H_{c'}^eM$ already lives over $Y'$; there is no further pullback of $q'_M$.

Expand $J,T,D_{c',M}$ and cancel adjacent inverse comparisons. This gives
$$J_LT_L=H_{c'}^p(a_{g',L})C_{c',M}A_{Y'}(q'_M)=T^c_L A_{Y'}(q'_M).$$
Using the preceding two equations, associativity, and functorial preservation of composition and inverses,
$$\begin{aligned}J_L\Phi_Lp_g(D_{c,L})^{-1}
&=T^c_L A_{Y'}(q'_M E_L)S_L^{-1}p_g(D_{c,L})^{-1}\\
&=T^c_L A_{Y'}(E^c_L)A_{Y'}(l_gq_L)S_L^{-1}p_g(D_{c,L})^{-1}\\
&=T^c_L A_{Y'}(E^c_L)(S^c_L)^{-1}=\Phi^c_L.
\end{aligned}$$
This is an algebraic cancellation of isomorphisms already established; neither $E$ nor $\Phi$ is cancelled.

source.place: Transport paragraph: explicit endpoint conjugation calculation

proof.text:
For restriction write $i:V\hookrightarrow Y$, $i':V'=g^{-1}V\hookrightarrow Y'$, $i_X:X_V\hookrightarrow X$, $N=l_{i_X}L$, and let $\square_V$ denote the restricted square. Write $\bar E=l_{i'}E_L$. Under canonical composite-pullback identifications, the restriction law in [lem-cbc-etale-local-compact-support-extension] states
$$\tau\bar E=E^V_N\sigma,\qquad\sigma=l_{g_V}(r^f_{V,L}),\quad\tau=r^{f'}_{V',l_{g'}L}.$$
For $A=A_{V'}$ define the two endpoint isomorphisms
$$K_s=p_{i'}(S_L)a_{i',l_gH_fL},\qquad K_t=p_{i'}(T_L)a_{i',H_{f'}l_{g'}L}.$$
Naturality of $a_{i'}$ [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] and the definition of $\Phi$ give $p_{i'}(\Phi_L)=K_tA(\bar E)K_s^{-1}$. The endpoint identifications to the restricted formulas are therefore
$$U=S^V_N A(\sigma)K_s^{-1},\qquad W=T^V_N A(\tau)K_t^{-1}.$$
They use exactly $r,a,C_f,C_{f'}$. Cancelling $K_s,K_t$ now gives
$$W p_{i'}(\Phi_L)U^{-1}=T^V_N A(\tau\bar E\sigma^{-1})(S^V_N)^{-1}=\Phi^V_N.$$
Applying steps 4--6 to $\square_V$ proves the chart normalization after inserting these endpoint identifications.

For two successive open restrictions, substitute the formulas for $U$ and $W$ of step 7. In the composite endpoint, the intermediate $S^V$ (respectively $T^V$) and its inverse cancel. The remaining two $A(\sigma)$ factors multiply to the single $A(\sigma)$ for the composite restriction, and likewise for $A(\tau)$, by the iterated-restriction law for $r$ in [lem-cbc-etale-local-compact-support-extension]. The remaining $a$ factors are those for the composite by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. Thus the endpoints for successive restrictions equal the endpoints for their composite. Identity restrictions give identities. On each restricted square, use its own specified chart comparisons $q,C_c,D,J$ in steps 4--6; step 7 inserts the coherent endpoints $U,W$ into that chart equation. This proves all asserted restriction coherence without requiring that an arbitrary open restriction itself be quasi-compact.
